summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, gastritis, and prior bladder tumor resection was admitted for chest and abdominal pain. Evaluation revealed no cardiac cause for chest pain, which resolved spontaneously, and imaging showed right lower lobe opacities consistent with pneumonia, for which oral levofloxacin was initiated. Abdominal pain was attributed to alcoholic gastritis, worsened by recent alcohol use, and managed with omeprazole and supportive care. The patient had chronic anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.1 on admission, believed to be due to multiple sources including gastritis, hematuria, and colonic angiectasias, with a low reticulocyte count suggesting inadequate red blood cell production. He was counseled on alcohol cessation and discharged home on day two with stable symptoms, instructions to follow up with primary care for anemia workup, and completion of antibiotic therapy.
